program_plain: World: a 64x64 lattice of cells (wrap-around edges, 8 neighbours each). Cells have 3 types (type 0 = empty, 5% of cells; random start). Rules each step: an occupied cell whose same-type share among occupied neighbours is below 0.9 moves to a random empty cell.
model_family: Schelling segregation model (agent-based / statistical physics of vacancy-mediated coarsening)
standard_name: Schelling segregation / spatial clustering and coarsening (high-intolerance, active/mixed regime)
citations: Dall'Asta, Castellano & Marsili 2008, J. Stat. Mech. L07002 (arXiv:0707.1681) - statistical physics of Schelling model: coarsening, kinetic constrained transitions, percolation
Vinkovic & Kirman 2006, PNAS 103(51):19261-19265 - physical analogue of Schelling model; surface-tension-driven cluster dynamics, large segregated domains or frozen clusters
Aging effects in Schelling segregation model 2022, Sci. Rep. - describes frozen/segregated/mixed phases and mixed-state transition near T=0.75 in the standard two-type model; power-law coarsening
Gauvin, Vannimenus & Nadal 2009, Eur. Phys. J. B 70, 293 - phase diagram of Schelling model (seen only in reference lists, not opened)
searches: Schelling segregation model statistical physics coarsening domains vacancy Dall'Asta Castellano Marsili
Vinkovic Kirman physical analogue of the Schelling model PNAS 2006
Schelling model high tolerance threshold never freezes unhappy agents interface dynamics multiple types
notes: Clustering is firmly known. Not verified: the exact 3-type, blind random relocation, threshold 0.9 combination; the rising-activity metric; and the 'one type fills the lattice' reading (likely largest connected same-type cluster). Published physics papers mostly use 2 types and satisfaction-seeking moves. At threshold 0.9 the literature suggests a persistently active, possibly mixed regime and not full segregation.
full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** This is the Schelling segregation model, and the clustering is its textbook result. Confidence is medium. The 3-type, blind-relocation, threshold-0.9 details are not covered by anything I read, and neither is the "activity rising" metric.

**1. Model family.** The system is the Schelling segregation model, a lattice model with vacancies and threshold-based relocation. It comes from social physics and agent-based modelling, and statistical physics has since treated it as a vacancy-mediated coarsening or kinetic-constrained model. Here the lattice has 5% vacancies, three types, 8 neighbours and wrap-around edges. A cell is unhappy if its same-type share is below 0.9, and unhappy cells jump to a random empty cell.

**2. The behaviour in the literature.**
- **Clustering and coarsening.** Schelling's simple relocation rule produces strong spatial clustering, which shows up here as high Moran's I. It is the model's defining result.
  - Earliest clear source I verified: Dall'Asta, Castellano & Marsili, "Statistical physics of the Schelling model of segregation", J. Stat. Mech. 2008, L07002 (arXiv:0707.1681). It reports static phase transitions typical of kinetic constrained models, nontrivial coarsening like in driven-particle systems, and percolation-related phenomena. The paper notes that segregation in the Schelling model resembles the coarsening processes of phase-separation kinetics.
  - Earlier physics-style treatment: Vinković & Kirman, "A physical analogue of the Schelling model", PNAS 103(51):19261–19265, 2006. Cluster dynamics is driven by "surface tension", and the segregated areas can be very large and behave like liquid droplets or frozen clusters.
  - Schelling's own 1969 and 1971 papers are the originals. I only saw them cited in the results, so I have not verified them.
- **Review and context.**
  - Dall'Asta et al. is the nearest thing to a review of the physics that I read.
  - The Gauvin, Vannimenus & Nadal 2009 phase-diagram paper (Eur. Phys. J. B 70, 293) appears in the reference lists I saw, but I did not open it.
  - A later Scientific Reports paper, "Aging effects in Schelling segregation model" (2022), describes the phases of the standard model. There are three phases: frozen, segregated and mixed. Low tolerance freezes in a disordered state, and increasing tolerance gives a segregated state with two clusters. That paper reports a transition to a mixed state at T = 0.75 in the two-type case.
- **Threshold 0.9 and the "active" regime.** A threshold of 0.9 is a very intolerant setting. With 8 neighbours, a cell with one differing neighbour has a same-type share of 7/8 = 0.875, which is below 0.9, so it is unhappy. Cells are only happy inside pure-type regions, so interface cells are always unhappy and keep moving. The system therefore never freezes and stays active. This matches the literature's picture of persistent dynamics at high intolerance, where a satisfied state is never reached. The 0.85 variant is in the same regime, because 7/8 = 0.875 is still above 0.85.

**3. Differences from the published systems (why this isn't a stronger "known").**
- Dall'Asta et al. and Gauvin et al. use two types and move agents only to vacancies that satisfy them, or only if utility increases. Here three types are used and unhappy cells jump blindly to a random empty cell. Blind random relocation is a recognised Schelling variant (it resembles noise or "random relocation" versions), but I did not find a source for exactly this rule. I expect it matters quantitatively, for example for the activity level, and not for the qualitative clustering.
- I did not find a source for the exact 3-type, 5%-vacancy, 0.9-threshold combination.
- "One cell-type fills most of the lattice" (g_largest_domain) cannot literally hold with three roughly equal types. It probably means the largest connected same-type cluster is large, which fits coarsening into a few big domains, possibly percolating. At high intolerance the literature points to a mixed or active phase and not clean full segregation, so this metric deserves a check.
- "Activity rising" (g_activity_trend) is the one feature I could not match to a specific paper. The Schelling literature usually reports unhappy-agent counts or interface density decaying as coarsening proceeds. A rising or sustained activity measure is plausible for blind relocation at a threshold this high, but it is not documented in what I read.

**4. Confidence: medium.** The clustering and coarsening behaviour is firmly established and I verified the sources. The uncertainty is in the variant details above.
